subject: Literature
title: Margaret Atwood and Feminist Myth
description: A micro-lesson that makes Margaret Atwood and Feminist Myth usable.

hook.text: Margaret Atwood retold the Odyssey from Penelope's perspective, giving voice to the wife left waiting at home.

buildup.text: The Penelopiad revealed that the twelve maids Odysseus hanged were silenced victims, not guilty servants.

discovery.text: Atwood joined a wave of feminist writers rewriting myths from the perspectives of forgotten women.

twist.text: Madeline Miller's Circe and Pat Barker's The Silence of the Girls continued this mythic feminist revolution.

climax.text: Feminist retellings proved that who tells the myth determines whose truth the world remembers.

punchline.text: The women in myths finally got to tell their version.

quiz.question: What did Atwood's The Penelopiad do with Homer's Odyssey?
options: It translated the Odyssey into modern English
It retold the story from Penelope's perspective, giving voice to silenced women
It continued the Odyssey with a sequel about Odysseus's next voyage
